body.statement: For every \(n\ge1\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_+}\mathbb P_P\!\left(B_\pi(u,v)\in\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] If \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0\), then on \(\{\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\}\), every element of \(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\) has the true label and \[\operatorname{diam}_\infty(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha))\le2L_\star\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=O(n^{-1/2}).\] These conclusions hold for every rank of \(\operatorname{Var}_P(\operatorname{vech}(X^{\otimes3}))\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), an integer \(n\geq 1\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  We first establish the uniform support bound required for concentration.  For a representation of \(P\) supplied by \(\texttt{def:positive-model}\), the structural equation in \(\texttt{ass:structural-equation}\) gives, in the causal order \(\pi=(a,b,c)\),
\[
X_a=xH+s_a\xi_a,\qquad
X_b=uX_a+yH+s_b\xi_b,\qquad
X_c=vX_b+zH+s_c\xi_c.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:source-support}\), \(\texttt{ass:positive-mechanism-box}\), and \(\texttt{ass:residual-scale-box}\),
\[
|X_a|
 \leq 2(x+s_a)
 \leq 2\left(\frac34+\frac54\right)=4,
\]
\[
|X_b|
 \leq u|X_a|+2(y+s_b)
 \leq \frac34\,4+2\left(\frac34+\frac54\right)=7,
\]
and
\[
|X_c|
 \leq v|X_b|+2(z+s_c)
 \leq \frac34\,7+2\left(\frac34+\frac54\right)
 =\frac{37}{4}=R_X.
\]
Thus \(\max_{i\in\mathcal V}|X_i|\leq R_X\) almost surely, independently of the particular labeling \(\pi\).  By \(\texttt{ass:source-centering}\) and linearity of the structural equation, \(\mathbb E_P[X]=0\).  Substitution into the defining formula for a third joint cumulant therefore gives
\[
C_{ijk}=\operatorname{Cum}(X_i,X_j,X_k)=\mathbb E_P[X_iX_jX_k].
\]

Fix one of the ten triples \(1\leq i\leq j\leq k\leq 3\), and set
\[
Z_\ell=X_i^{(\ell)}X_j^{(\ell)}X_k^{(\ell)},
\qquad 1\leq\ell\leq n.
\]
The sampling assumption \(\texttt{ass:iid-sampling}\) makes \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) independent, and the preceding support bound gives
\[
-R_X^3\leq Z_\ell\leq R_X^3\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Apply \(\texttt{lem:hoeffding-bounded-sum}\) first to \(Z_\ell\) and then to \(-Z_\ell\), with deviation \(n\varepsilon\).  Using \(\texttt{def:empirical-cubic}\) and the identity for \(C_{ijk}\), we obtain, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_P\!\left(
 |\widehat C_{ijk}-C_{ijk}|>\varepsilon
\right)
&\leq
2\exp\!\left{
-\frac{2n^2\varepsilon^2}{n(2R_X^3)^2}
\right}\\
&=2\exp\!\left(-\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{2R_X^6}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
A union bound over the ten distinct coordinates of the symmetric cubic tensor yields
\[
\mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \|\widehat C-C\|_\infty>\varepsilon
\right)
\leq
20\exp\!\left(-\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{2R_X^6}\right).
\]
At
\[
\varepsilon=\varepsilon_n(\alpha)
=R_X^3\sqrt{\frac{2\log(20/\alpha)}{n}},
\]
the right-hand side is exactly \(\alpha\).  Define
\[
\mathcal E_n=
\{\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\}.
\]
The parameter \(\theta\) generating \(P\) belongs to \(\Theta_+\) by \(\texttt{def:positive-model}\) and \(\texttt{def:positive-parameter-set}\), while \(\texttt{lem:cubic-factorization}\) gives \(\Phi_+(\theta)=C\).  Hence, on \(\mathcal E_n\), the definition \(\texttt{def:confidence-set}\) includes the true matrix:
\[
B_\pi(u,v)\in\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha).
\]
Since the concentration bound is independent of \(P\),
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_+}
\mathbb P_P\!\left(B_\pi(u,v)\in\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\right)
\geq
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_+}\mathbb P_P(\mathcal E_n)
\geq 1-\alpha.
\]

It remains to prove the deterministic diameter assertion.  Let
\[
C^{(r)}=\Phi_+(\theta^{(r)}),\qquad
\theta^{(r)}\in\Theta_+,qquad r\in\{0,1\},
\]
and put \(\eta=\|C^{(0)}-C^{(1)}\|_\infty\).  Proposition \(\texttt{prop:source-feasibility}\) supplies, separately for each of the four entries of the skewness vector in \(\theta^{(r)}\), an independent bounded, centered, unit-variance source with the prescribed third cumulant.  Together with the remaining coordinates of \(\theta^{(r)}\), these sources define a law \(P_r\in\mathcal P_+\); by \(\texttt{lem:cubic-factorization}\), its cubic tensor is \(C^{(r)}\).  Consequently the support calculation above applies to both \(P_r\), and every entry of \(C^{(r)}\), hence of every associated slice, has absolute value at most
\[
K_0=R_X^3.
\]

We record perturbation inequalities that use only this entrywise bound.  If \(|q_j|,|q'_j|\leq K_0\) and \(|q_j-q'_j|\leq\eta\) for \(j=1,2,3\), telescoping the product gives
\[
|q_1q_2q_3-q'_1q'_2q'_3|
\leq 3K_0^2\eta.
\]
A \(3\)-by-\(3\) determinant is a signed sum of six such products, and an adjugate entry is a signed sum of two products of two entries.  Thus, for any pair of corresponding slices \(M,M'\),
\[
|\det(M)-\det(M')|\leq18K_0^2\eta,
\qquad
\|\operatorname{adj}(M)-\operatorname{adj}(M')\|_\infty
\leq4K_0\eta.
\]
For any fixed coordinate \(c\), let \(N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c\) and \(N'=\operatorname{adj}(M'_a)e_c\).  The two-term cofactor formula and the preceding inequality imply
\[
\|N\|_\infty,\|N'\|_\infty\leq2K_0^2,
\qquad
\|N-N'\|_\infty\leq4K_0\eta.
\]
On a common labeled chart, put \(W=M_bN\) and \(W'=M'_bN'\).  Expanding each of the three terms in a row--column product gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|W-W'\|_\infty
&\leq3\left(\eta\,2K_0^2+K_0\,4K_0\eta\right)
=18K_0^2\eta,\\
\|W\|_\infty,\|W'\|_\infty
&\leq3K_0(2K_0^2)=6K_0^3.
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally define on that chart
\[
D=N_bW_b+N_cW_c,
\quad D'=N'_bW'_b+N'_cW'_c,
\quad A=-N_aW_b,
\quad A'=-N'_aW'_b.
\]
For each product, add and subtract the cross term.  The displayed bounds then give
\[
|A-A'|
\leq (4K_0\eta)(6K_0^3)+(2K_0^2)(18K_0^2\eta)
=60K_0^4\eta
\]
and, because \(D\) contains two such products,
\[
|D-D'|\leq120K_0^4\eta.
\]

We now show that the six labeled images are uniformly separated.  Suppose first that the root labels of \(C^{(0)}\) and \(C^{(1)}\) differ, and let \(a_0\) denote the root of \(C^{(0)}\).  Theorem \(\texttt{thm:global-cubic-inverse}\) gives
\[
\det(M_{a_0}^{(0)})=0,
\qquad
|\det(M_{a_0}^{(1)})|\geq\min(d_b,d_c),
\]
because \(a_0\) is a nonroot label for the second tensor.  The determinant perturbation inequality therefore implies
\[
\eta\geq\frac{\min(d_b,d_c)}{18K_0^2}.
\]
Suppose next that the roots agree, equal to \(a\), but the middle labels differ.  Let \(j\) be the middle label for \(C^{(0)}\); with three labels, \(j\) is the terminal label for \(C^{(1)}\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:adjugate-sign-margin}\), applied to the two laws \(P_0,P_1\), yields
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a^{(0)})\bigr)_{aj}\leq-m,
\qquad
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a^{(1)})\bigr)_{aj}\geq m.
\]
Combining their difference, of magnitude at least \(2m\), with the adjugate perturbation inequality gives
\[
2m\leq4K_0\eta,
\qquad
\eta\geq\frac{m}{2K_0}.
\]
By the definition of \(\delta_0\), these two cases prove
\[
\|C^{(0)}-C^{(1)}\|_\infty<\delta_0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\theta^{(0)}\text{ and }\theta^{(1)}\text{ have the same label }(a,b,c).
\]

On a fixed label chart, \(\texttt{thm:global-cubic-inverse}\) gives
\[
|W_b|,|W'_b|\geq d_W,
\qquad
|D|,|D'|\geq d_D,
\qquad
v=\frac{W_c}{W_b},\quad v'=\frac{W'_c}{W'_b},
\qquad
u=\frac{A}{D},\quad u'=\frac{A'}{D'}.
\]
The coefficient box further gives \(|u'|,|v'|\leq3/4\).  For nonzero \(q,q'\), the identity
\[
\frac{p}{q}-\frac{p'}{q'}
=\frac{p-p'-(p'/q')(q-q')}{q}
\]
implies
\[
\left|\frac{p}{q}-\frac{p'}{q'}\right|
\leq\frac{|p-p'|+|p'/q'|\,|q-q'|}{|q|}.
\]
Apply this first to \(v=W_c/W_b\), using the bound on \(W-W'\), and then to \(u=A/D\), using the bounds on \(A-A'\) and \(D-D'\).  This yields
\[
|v-v'|
\leq
\frac{18K_0^2+(3/4)18K_0^2}{d_W}\eta
=\frac{63K_0^2}{2d_W}\eta
\]
and
\[
|u-u'|
\leq
\frac{60K_0^4+(3/4)120K_0^4}{d_D}\eta
=\frac{150K_0^4}{d_D}\eta.
\]
Since on a common chart the two nonzero entries of \(B_\pi(u,v)-B_\pi(u',v')\) are precisely \(u-u'\) and \(v-v'\), the definition of \(L_\star\) gives the deterministic implication
\[
\|C^{(0)}-C^{(1)}\|_\infty<\delta_0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\|B_{\pi^{(0)}}(u^{(0)},v^{(0)})-B_{\pi^{(1)}}(u^{(1)},v^{(1)})\|_\infty
\leq L_\star\|C^{(0)}-C^{(1)}\|_\infty,
\]
with equality of the two labels already established on the left-hand regime.

Assume finally that \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0\) and that \(\mathcal E_n\) occurs.  If a parameter \(\theta'\in\Theta_+\) is retained by \(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\), then \(\texttt{def:confidence-set}\) and the triangle inequality give
\[
\|\Phi_+(\theta')-C\|_\infty
\leq
\|\Phi_+(\theta')-\widehat C\|_\infty
+\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty
\leq2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0.
\]
The chart-separation implication proves that every retained parameter has the true label.  Moreover, for any two retained parameters \(\theta^{(0)},\theta^{(1)}\),
\[
\|\Phi_+(\theta^{(0)})-\Phi_+(\theta^{(1)})\|_\infty
\leq2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0.
\]
Applying the fixed-chart Lipschitz inequality and then taking the supremum over the two retained matrices proves
\[
\operatorname{diam}_\infty(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha))
\leq2L_\star\varepsilon_n(\alpha).
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\), the definition of \(\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\) makes the right-hand side \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Every probabilistic step above used only boundedness and independence across observations, and every inversion step used only the deterministic denominator bounds from \(\texttt{thm:global-cubic-inverse}\).  No inverse, rank condition, or nonsingularity assumption was imposed on \(\operatorname{Var}_P(\operatorname{vech}(X^{\otimes3}))\).  The coverage and diameter conclusions therefore hold for every rank of that covariance matrix.
body.justification: The set gives honest uncertainty quantification across discrete order selection and rational denominators without a Wald approximation.
body.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025) provide point estimators but no coverage theorem; Babii (2020) and Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) do not treat a finite union of exact LvLiNGAM charts.
body.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can return a certified effect set and an order-ambiguity warning even when empirical moment covariance is singular.
